evidence.description: Google documents HTTPS event collection at www.google-analytics.com/mp/collect and region1.google-analytics.com/mp/collect.
Google's troubleshooting guide identifies google-analytics.com/g/collect requests as Analytics collection traffic.

Google lists analytics.google.com/g/collect as an Analytics request endpoint. The hostname is kept in review status because a domain match alone does not establish which application initiated a request or what data it sent.

Microsoft's Clarity setup guide identifies POST requests to https://www.clarity.ms/collect as Clarity collection traffic. The hostname match identifies a known service endpoint; it does not prove which app initiated the request or what any payload contained.

PostHog's event-capture troubleshooting documentation names us.i.posthog.com and eu.i.posthog.com as hosted API hosts. Self-hosted deployments or custom API hosts will not necessarily match; a match does not establish which data was sent.

Google's Google tag setup guide recommends checking requests to googleadservices.com or googlesyndication.com when verifying Google Ads tags. These are broad advertising-service domains; blocking them may affect ad-supported or conversion-related functionality and is not proof of personalized ads.

Google's Google tag setup guide lists doubleclick.net as a destination to inspect when verifying Floodlight traffic. The domain is broad and can be shared across services, so it remains review-only and is not imported by the active-indicator action.

Pinterest's official Tag documentation includes https://ct.pinterest.com/v3/ pixel URLs for page-view and conversion events. A hostname match identifies a documented tag endpoint, not the initiating app or full payload.

Amplitude documents api2.amplitude.com as the default HTTP V2 event-ingestion host and api.eu.amplitude.com for EU data residency. SDKs may use different paths or configurable proxies; a hostname match does not establish payload contents or the initiating app.

Segment's official engineering article documents Analytics.js track/identify calls sending data to api.segment.io and describes its Tracking API. First-party proxies, regional/custom endpoints, and server-side forwarding may not match; the domain does not reveal which properties were sent.

AppsFlyer's official troubleshooting documentation recommends the appsflyersdk.com endpoint for SDK traffic to ensure TLS 1.2/1.3 in the described iOS configuration. This supports an association with SDK communication but not an exclusive attribution-only purpose across all deployments; kept review-only pending broader endpoint-scope review.

entries.name: Mixpanel event and profile ingestion endpoints

evidence.description: Mixpanel's official Track Event API documents the event-ingestion endpoint. Mixpanel's official tracking-proxy documentation describes api.mixpanel.com as the default host and api-eu.mixpanel.com/api-in.mixpanel.com for EU/India residency. Regional selection, custom proxies, and SDK changes can alter the observed host; a hostname match does not reveal event contents.

entries.name: Adjust click and impression attribution endpoints

evidence.description: Adjust's official link documentation distinguishes app.adjust.com click endpoints from view.adjust.com impression/connected-TV endpoints. These are attribution-link endpoints; a hostname match does not establish which app initiated it or what identifiers were transmitted.

entries.name: BugSnag error and session reporting endpoints

evidence.description: BugSnag's Android configuration documentation identifies notify.bugsnag.com and sessions.bugsnag.com as its default hosted error-report and session endpoints, with custom endpoints available for on-premise deployments. A hostname match does not prove an app uploaded a report or reveal its contents.

entries.name: Branch mobile linking and attribution API

evidence.description: Branch's official API reference documents api2.branch.io as the API base URL and describes event tracking and attribution APIs. Because the host serves multiple Branch functions, the indicator remains review-only rather than being treated as a dedicated tracker endpoint.

Sentry's official self-hosted reverse-proxy documentation identifies organization-specific hosts such as o123456789.ingest.de.sentry.io and the /api/<project-id>/envelope/ endpoint as SDK event-ingestion paths. The catalog stores the parent domain only as a review indicator because regional and organization-specific hosts vary and sentry.io also covers unrelated Sentry services.
